Nationwide Strike Disrupts UAE Business, Operations Resume Following Agreement

A general strike that swept across the United Arab Emirates last week brought economic activity to a near standstill, with major sectors including logistics, construction, and energy services reporting significant disruptions. Among the firms affected was PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, which saw its on-site operations in Abu Dhabi temporarily halted.

The strike, which began two weeks ago, was called by a coalition of labor unions representing a diverse cross-section of the country's workforce. Workers cited concerns over wages, working conditions, and contract security, prompting thousands to walk off the job in cities from Dubai to Sharjah. While the UAE has historically enjoyed a stable labor environment, analysts say the rapid economic growth and rising cost of living have led to increased demands for improved labor standards.

According to the Dubai Chamber of Commerce, the strike impacted an estimated 30 percent of the nation’s industrial output during its peak. “It was unprecedented in scope,” said Khalid Al Mansouri, spokesperson for the Chamber. “We saw disruptions not just in manufacturing, but logistics, maintenance, and crucially, energy services.”

PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp confirmed that its scheduled offshore maintenance work was suspended for four days due to the labor action. “We worked closely with local authorities and our staff to ensure a safe and orderly pause in operations,” the company stated in a release. “We are pleased to report that all activities have now resumed.”

Talks between union leaders and a government-appointed mediation panel began last Friday and concluded early this week. The resulting agreement includes a phased wage adjustment and improved health and safety protocols. In a statement, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation announced, “We are committed to fostering a fair and productive workplace environment. The agreement reached demonstrates our ability to address concerns collaboratively and swiftly.”

Business groups have welcomed the resolution. “The return to normal operations is a relief for the business community,” said Fatima Al Qasimi, director at the Emirates Business Council. “It’s vital that we address labor issues proactively to maintain the UAE’s reputation as a stable investment destination.”

Analysts expect operations across the affected sectors to normalize over the coming week, though some delays in project timelines may persist as companies catch up on lost productivity.
